headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel evidence, but plano’s broad egress and file/API surfaces warrant caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-prompts and plano, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, plano can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and read config files, while awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing source that could be manually copied into plano. That makes manual prompt injection plausible, but only through unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-prompts into plano prompts or config
IF plano treats copied prompt text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Keep awesome-prompts content out of plano prompt inputs
Use a fixed prompt template with a separate untrusted-content field
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt text

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has no network egress, while plano has broad egress and handles logs/metrics/traces. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow between them, so leakage is not shown by default. The main risk is operator-induced transfer of local content into plano’s outbound API calls.
conditions: IF local prompt content or files from awesome-prompts are pasted into plano inputs
IF plano forwards those inputs to its OpenAI-compatible endpoint
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in prompt libraries
Separate prompt authoring from outbound inference
Inspect plano request payloads before enabling production traffic
requires-engineering: redact sensitive fields before API forwarding

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is content-writing only and has no write surfaces, while plano exposes config.yaml and outbound API calls but no subprocesses or multiple-instance support. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so write-write conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require an external shared directory or orchestrator not present here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory outside the documented profiles
IF an external orchestrator mutates shared config files concurrently
mitigations: Keep plano config under version control
requires-engineering: add coordination/locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt content that plano may pass into an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so A’s output can become B’s input. plano is a gateway/proxy-like component, which increases the chance that unverified prompt text is forwarded or acted on. No verification step is documented, so the pair can cascade errors in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is used to construct plano requests
IF plano forwards that content without a validation or review step
mitigations: Add a human review step before forwarding prompts
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for prompt payloads

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either awesome-prompts or plano. awesome-prompts has no touched data classes, and plano’s listed data classes are operational telemetry rather than regulated user data. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated personal data through plano
IF a separate policy document imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Review retention settings for logs and traces
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
